summary.text: Zyra is a modular Python framework for scientific and environmental data workflows, useful for importing, processing, visualizing, and exporting structured data in a reproducible manner. It becomes a poor fit for use cases outside this domain, applications requiring real-time streaming or tight integration with non-data systems, or projects where modularity and reproducibility are not priorities.

summary.text: Use the acquire http command, passing the URL as a positional argument and specifying the local destination with --output. This fetches a file over HTTP or HTTPS and writes it to the path you choose.

A repo-advisor outage would not break Orbit's science conversations. Orbit runs a hybrid architecture: an LLM streams a richer response in parallel with a local keyword engine that is always available and requires no network. If the LLM path is unavailable, the service transparently falls back to the local engine. The repo-advisor integration is a separate, proposed future capability and is not part of that fallback chain today.

This is a Terraviz-side change. Zyra produces the converted data; Terraviz owns the metadata schema and validation logic that is rejecting it. The contract to satisfy lives in the Terraviz catalog validators and dataset-mutations layer, not in Zyra's output pipeline.

costBasis: Published operator-supplied base token prices, estimated from reported usage. Not billed cost; excludes smoke calls, caching adjustments, discounts, taxes, and absent usage. Workers AI internal aliases are reported separately from requested endpoint tariffs.

selectionDecision.reason: All four configurations retain substantial rejection rates and accepted semantic or task-completion failures. Do not choose by guard rate, speed or price alone. Runtime continues to require explicit provider/model configuration.

nextDevelopmentCandidate.reason: Fastest and lowest base-token estimate in both new cohorts; v3 fixes the outage guarantee and service submission boundary in this sample. Still fails integration-plan usefulness and some factual/citation boundaries, so this is a development candidate, not an operational default.

selectionDecision.nextWork: Move service-boundary and proposed-integration answers into deterministic server-owned responses or enforceable contracts; improve integration-specific answer completeness; verify argument prerequisites and same-claim option evidence. Evaluate on additional held-out questions and then rerun this snapshot. Further prompt-only iterations on these same 24 questions are not enough to establish a safe default.
